Elijah the Tishbite. One of the most powerful prophets in Hebrew scripture, known for his dramatic confrontations with idolatry and his miraculous deeds during a period of spiritual apostasy in the northern kingdom of Israel.

He confronted King Ahab and Queen Jezebel over their promotion of Baal worship and their persecution of God's prophets. He challenged the prophets of Baal to a test on Mount Carmel: each side would prepare a sacrifice, and the true god would consume it with fire. God's fire consumed Elijah's offering, vindicating him.

He called down fire from heaven multiple times, including to consume a captain and his soldiers sent to arrest him. He declared a three-year drought over Israel as punishment for idolatry, then later prayed for rain to end it. During the drought, he was fed by ravens at the brook Cherith and sustained by a widow in Zarephath, demonstrating God's provision.

In a unique fate, Elijah was taken up to heaven in a chariot of fire in a whirlwind, never experiencing death, making him a symbol of eschatological hope. Before his ascension, he mentored Elisha, his successor, passing on his mantle and prophetic authority. His ministry is recorded in First Kings chapters seventeen through nineteen and Second Kings chapters one and two.
